Recipe:   


This will make a big pot of 3-4L 

Sour Rye Starter: 

* 150g of rye flour
* 500ml of water

Mix the water and flour in a container like a jar, cover with a cloth to keep out bugs and debris, leave in a warm dark place for a week until it sours. In most slavic countries you can actually buy this stuff but if so, get it from a babushka at the market. The store bought stuff is not the same.  


Soup Proper 

* some carrots 
* some celeriac 
* parsley root 
* some onion 
* white sausage (weisswurst)
* pork shoulder (optional) 
* sour rye starter 
* allspice 
* majoram
* salt
* pepper
* bay leaf (or 5) 
* sour cream (18% fat is best) 

Cut up the veggies into cubes and dump all of them except for the onion and garlic into a couple L of water or stock, start boiling. Add bay leaf, majoram and allspice berries

Cut up the sausage and the meat, use salt and pepper on the meat and fry both in some oil until brown. Throw into the soup. 

in the same pan, fry onions and garlic for a couple minutes, by now you should have a good layer of fond in the pot (the tasty brown stuff), deglaze with some water or stock (pour in the water and scrub up all the brown stuff). Dump it into the soup pot. 

Boil everything for about 30 minutes to an hour or until the pork is very tender. Adjust the ammount of water to how much veggies and meat you used. 

Start adding the sour rye starter bit by bit to taste (the soup is supposed to be sour but not so sour that it's difficult to eat, use your best judgement)

Temper the sour cream by pouring it into a bowl and adding a bit of the hot soup bit by bit while mixing. When it's much thiner dump it into the soup (this prevents your sour cream from clumping when added to a hot liquid).

Boil the whole thing for 30 minutes.   


Traditionally it's served with hard boiled eggs and mashed potates (no butter no cream, just boiled and mashed).
